question: What does the validated known-bot transform deliver across ingress, spoofing and configuration-drift conditions?
expressionValidation: Actual zone dashboard reports Rule validation passed for to_string(cf.client.bot), dynamic Set, with contradictory host filter; form cancelled unsaved.
signalMeaning: Generic provider known-good-bot/crawler assessment; not a signed-agent verdict, product identity, purpose or human label.
trust: Untrusted header observation only. No assignment to native booleans, classifier, authorization or public verified-bot counts.
prerequisites: Off-by-default dedicated non-HTML route, native-local tested before publication; no page collector invocation or observation writes on success or rejection.
At most fifteen minutes, registered control IDs and accepted existing exclusion/guard mechanism; expired human window stays expired.
Prepare exact rule scope and source before activation; time guard in both rule expression and receiver; initial state disabled.
Retain rule order/configuration and exact private control references; no credentials or raw diagnostics in Git.
Inventory actually available ingress and controlled relay prerequisites. Missing routes stay unexecuted, not passing.
No new plan, permission, credential, provider enrollment or third-party action inferred from this plan.
Genuine vendor-positive case needs its own eligible guard/control. Do not mark unrelated vendor traffic as owner traffic to manufacture acceptance.

capture.wireMultiplicity: Client harness records what it sent; Worker captures only resulting closed state. Header coalescing can erase wire multiplicity.
capture.publicOutput: Closed aggregate counts by condition; no trial IDs or account metadata.

conditions: Supplied true, false and malformed single headers
Duplicate headers in both value orders and comma-combined value
Rule disabled and rule absent, with supplied true
Rule time expired and receiver time expired
Controlled cross-zone relay, if available without broader access
Genuine provider-positive control, only with actual provider evidence; no impersonation or injected metadata

bounds.guardStorageCosts: If implementation reuses D1 guards, record native-tested and measured costs separately; zero diagnostic statements is not zero service cost.
bounds.logs: Exact control scope, private closed captures, stop owned tail after bounded run. Missing/sampled logs remain incomplete.
bounds.requestLimitEnforcement: Controller budget only; 32 registered controls do not globally limit repeat requests.

acceptance: Planned, executed, response-received, matched-log and eligible results have separate denominators.
Success and negative controls preserve no-collection boundary and expiry; no human label is generated.
Capture true/false/missing/malformed independently from configuration; literal true never authenticates itself.
Native-positive and unavailable ingress prerequisites are reported explicitly, with rates null where denominator is zero.
No trusted adoption follows automatically: configuration checks and marker headers cannot attest each request during drift/bypass.
Activation, natural expiry, configuration cleanup and persistence/retention are separate recorded operations.
managedSignatureComparison: Still blocked on the separate request-level signed-agent oracle and accepted controlled identity; this generic bit does not satisfy either gate.
nextBoundedAction: Accept article publication, then reconcile the retained-data delta since the frozen census using native-tested bounded SQL and an explicit D1 read budget. Genuine positive/relay and human gates remain open.

failureDiagnostics.activation: accepted; off-mode only; new reasons not observed in production
